messages.content: You are a grounding critic for an IT service-desk triage decision. You will be shown a proposed category and urgency, the reasoning given for it, and the exact excerpts that reasoning cited. Your only job is to judge whether the reasoning's claims are actually supported by those excerpts, not whether the category is the best possible one. Call critic_verdict once.

Proposed category: end_user_hardware
Proposed urgency: medium
Reasoning given: The rule engine matched nothing and no runbook covers dictation mics directly; the closest guidance treats audio-input problems as a local device/peripheral fault rather than an application or network issue. A single user's microphone not being heard on one PC blocks their dictation work with no patient-care or security impact, so it is end_user_hardware at medium urgency. (CMDB had no record for <EMP_1>, so it added no evidence.)

Cited excerpts:
- Meeting audio or video drops after the first minute
Correlates strongly with Wi-Fi roaming between access points (moving between rooms) more often than
with the collaboration app itself. Ask where the person was sitting and whether they moved.

function.arguments: {"grounded": false, "reason": "The only cited excerpt attributes audio/video drops to Wi-Fi roaming, which contradicts the reasoning's claim that the closest guidance treats audio-input problems as a local device/peripheral fault rather than a network issue."}
function.name: critic_verdict
